name: icons
note: UI icons (owner, 2026-11-01): the nav column and the header buttons, drawn as painted storybook icons in the world art's palette and light, to replace the emoji-style glyphs. refs/current-nav-icons.jpg is the set being replaced (the subjects, not the style). Three variants are the three directions offered in round 1.
preamble: A SHEET OF UI ICONS for a 2D fairy-tale farming RPG. The first {refCount} attached images are the game's own world art: STYLE REFERENCES for palette, light and brushwork only (warm earthy colours, cream, terracotta, mossy green, warm wood, amber accents; bright, warm daylight from the upper left; chunky hand-shaped forms). The icons are PLAYFUL and STORYBOOK: bouncy, slightly exaggerated, rounded proportions, a little crooked, cheerful, never corporate, never a flat pictogram, never an emoji. Each icon is ONE bold, simple object that reads instantly at thumbnail size (it will be shown 28 pixels tall): one strong silhouette, big simple shapes, few details, no tiny parts, no background, no ground, no scene. All the icons on the sheet share ONE consistent size (each fills about two thirds of its cell), ONE consistent light, ONE consistent rendering, so they clearly belong to one set. The LAST attached image is the layout guide: a pure magenta (#FF00FF) field divided into a grid of equal cells by thin lines; draw exactly ONE icon in the CENTRE of each cell, in the order given (left to right, then top to bottom), never touching or crossing a cell line, leaving a clear magenta margin around every icon; leave every other pixel pure magenta, no grid lines drawn over the icons, no vignette. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no watermark, no frame.

variants.painted: RENDERING: soft painterly shading with a little surface texture, no outline, depth from light and shadow, a soft contact shadow directly under each object; exactly the rendering of the attached world art, so the icons look like small pieces of the world.
variants.sticker: RENDERING: the same painterly fill, but each icon is a STICKER: a thick, even, cream-white border runs around its whole silhouette with a thin dark edge outside that, like a die-cut sticker; proportions pushed chunkier and bouncier, a bright highlight dot on the main surface, no contact shadow; crisp and poppy, made to sit on a dark green button.
variants.inked: RENDERING: a dark warm-brown ink outline of even weight around every object and its major parts, flat fills with one shadow tone and one highlight per colour, a few confident line details, no texture, no contact shadow; like a hand-inked storybook plate; chunky, bold, cheerful.
variants.props: RENDERING: exactly the rendering of the attached world art: soft painterly shading, visible brushwork, no outline, no border, a soft contact shadow under each object; MUTED, earthy, grown-up colour (ochre, umber, slate, moss, oxblood, parchment), nothing candy-bright. Each icon is a real PROP from this world, drawn as a thing, not a cartoon: hand-made, a little worn, a little crooked, with character but NO faces drawn on objects and NO big cartoon eyes; animals drawn naturalistically with storybook charm.
variants.woodcut: RENDERING: an Elizabethan WOODCUT, like a printer's ornament from a First Folio or a hand-printed broadside: bold black ink with confident cut hatching for the shadows, white where the paper shows, and a flat hand-tinted wash of two or three muted colours laid loosely inside the lines (ochre, oxblood, moss, slate) the way old prints were coloured by hand; slightly uneven, charming, literary, never slick. No border, no background.
variants.tavern-sign: RENDERING: each icon is a small painted TAVERN SIGN: a round or shield-shaped wooden plaque with a worn, chipped painted rim and the object painted on it in the game's soft painterly style, a little weathered, the way the buildings in this game hang image-only signs; muted earthy paint, warm wood, a soft shadow under the plaque. All plaques the same size and shape so the set lines up.
variants.emblem: RENDERING: each icon is a GILDED EMBLEM: the object rendered as a raised relief on a round medallion of aged pewter or brass, with the object itself picked out in a muted enamel colour and the highlights touched with gold leaf, like a heraldic badge or a theatre's brass seat plaque; dignified, antique, lightly whimsical in its shapes; a soft shadow under the medallion. All medallions the same size.
variants.props-front: RENDERING: exactly the rendering of the attached world art: soft painterly shading, visible brushwork, no outline, no border, no plaque, no background; MUTED, earthy, grown-up colour (ochre, umber, slate, moss, oxblood, parchment), nothing candy-bright. SIMPLER than a painting: each icon is ONE object reduced to its biggest shapes, three or four colours, no small details, no texture noise, so it stays clean at 28 pixels. CAMERA, the same as the game's world art and NOT negotiable: every object is seen STRAIGHT FROM THE FRONT, flat-on, as if standing on a shelf at eye level facing the viewer, its front face parallel to the picture plane; NO three-quarter turn, NO perspective, NO foreshortening, NO tilted top faces, no isometric angle; symmetrical objects drawn symmetrically; a book seen from the front cover, a cottage from its front wall, a cup from its side. Light from the upper left, a thin soft contact shadow under each object. Real props from this world, a little hand-made and crooked, with character but NO faces drawn on objects and NO big cartoon eyes; animals drawn naturalistically in a flat side or front view.
variants.props-lit: RENDERING: the game's painterly look, SIMPLIFIED and in FULL DAYLIGHT. Simplify: each icon is ONE object reduced to its biggest shapes, three or four flat-ish colours per object, broad soft shading only, NO fine texture, NO grain, NO stitching, NO tiny ornament, NO small lettering or patterns, so it stays clean at 28 pixels; no outline, no border, no plaque, no background. Daylight: bright, sunny, warm light from high up and a little to the left, the whole front of every object clearly and evenly lit, colours clean and luminous (fresh carrot orange, sunny straw, warm honey wood, clean cream parchment, bright moss green, polished gold), NO murk, NO brown haze, NO dark shadow on the facing surfaces; shadows soft, short and only underneath; a thin soft contact shadow under each object. CAMERA, the same as the game's world art and NOT negotiable: every object seen STRAIGHT FROM THE FRONT, flat-on, its front face parallel to the picture plane; NO three-quarter turn, NO perspective, NO tilted top faces; symmetrical objects drawn symmetrically. Grown-up storybook props, a little hand-made and crooked, with character but NO faces drawn on objects and NO big cartoon eyes; animals naturalistic in a flat front view.
variants.system: RENDERING: SYSTEM-STYLE GLYPH ICONS, like a phone's own app and toolbar icons, drawn in the game's paint: each icon is one bold, simple, instantly familiar silhouette, the standard shape everyone knows for that function, NOT a detailed object and NOT a scene; generous rounded forms, thick strokes, no thin lines, no small parts, two or three colours at most (warm cream or honey wood for the body, one accent), a soft painterly fill with one gentle highlight and a short soft shadow beneath, no outline, no border, no plaque, no background; bright, clean, sunny; flat-on, symmetrical where the shape is symmetrical. The attached small image is the APPROVED exemplar: a cream speech bubble with three dots, that exact weight, simplicity and rendering for the whole set.
